chunk_findings.detail: The new line reads the enforcement knob with an unchecked attribute chain, while the very code it wraps in the same function deliberately guards exactly this lookup eight lines later: `policy = getattr(cfg, "enforce", None)` / `getattr(policy, "commit_without_lease", "warn") if policy else "warn"`. That guard exists because `cfg.enforce` can be absent/`None` and its keys can be missing (the sibling helper does the same for `cfg.flow`: `getattr(getattr(cfg, "flow", None), "environments", None)`). With a config that has no `[enforce]` section, or an `[enforce]` section that does not set `environment_commits` (i.e. every existing user before this change), `cfg.enforce` is `None` (or has no such attribute), so `cfg.enforce.environment_commits` raises `AttributeError`/`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute ...` before any branch or lease logic runs. The result is not "commit on an env branch is refused" but "every `git commit` in that repo dies with a traceback on a normal work branch", since the line executes unconditionally at the top of `check_commit`. It needs the same guarded/defaulted read used for `commit_without_lease` (with the documented `"block"` default).

chunk_findings.detail:
The single message string hard-codes `Policy is [enforce].environment_commits = "block" in .ddflow/config.toml; set it to "warn" or "off" ...`, but this same text is emitted in `warn` mode: with `environment_commits = "warn"` the early `return 1, env_msg` does not fire, `msg = "

".join(... env_msg + "

(warning only)" ...)` is returned, and the user is told the policy is `"block"` and advised to set it to `"warn"` or `"off"` — which is precisely what they have already configured. The message must be parameterised by the effective mode (or the policy sentence omitted in warn mode).

chunk_findings.detail: `test_check_commit_unit` writes the staged change with `_git(repo, "a.txt").write_text("hotfix\n")` instead of `(repo / "a.txt").write_text("hotfix\n")`, which is what every other test in this file uses. `_git` runs `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", <repo>, "a.txt"], check=True, ...)`, so git is invoked with `a.txt` as the subcommand. Git has no such command, so it exits non-zero, and because `_git`'s `check` defaults to `True` the call raises `subprocess.CalledProcessError` before `write_text` is ever reached (and even if `check` were `False`, it would return a `CompletedProcess`, which has no `write_text`, raising `AttributeError`). The consequence is that `a.txt` is never modified or staged and `E.check_commit(repo)` is never reached with a real uncommitted direct change: the test fails on the setup line regardless of whether the hook feature under review works. This is the only unit-level assertion of the `E.check_commit` return contract (`code == 1` and the message text), so the contract is effectively untested.

chunk_findings.detail: `check_commit` reads the new policy option through an unguarded attribute chain, while the half of the function it was just split from (`_check_lease`) deliberately guards the exact same access: `policy = getattr(cfg, "enforce", None)` … `mode = getattr(policy, "commit_without_lease", "warn") if policy else "warn"`. That guard exists because `cfg.enforce` is not guaranteed to be present/truthy — a config with no `[enforce]` table leaves it as `None`/absent, which is why the pre-existing code supplies a default instead of dereferencing. The new line dereferences it unconditionally, and also assumes `environment_commits` exists on whatever object `enforce` is (an older/laxer config object need not define it). Demonstrated input: a repo whose `.ddflow/config.toml` contains `[flow]` (with `environments = ["production"]`) but no `[enforce]` section, and `git commit -m x` on branch `main`. `check_commit` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'environment_commits'` (or `AttributeError` for the missing option) *before* the branch check is even reached; an exception out of a `pre-commit` hook is a non-zero exit, so the commit is refused — on a non-environment branch, with a config that never opted into the feature at all. The `env_mode != "off"` short-circuit does not help, because the failure happens while computing `env_mode`; the whole point of "off"/default-warn is defeated (every commit anywhere without `[enforce]` is blocked, which is stricter than `block`). Guard consistently with the sibling code, e.g. `getattr(getattr(cfg, "enforce", None), "environment_commits", "warn")`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py, `check_commit` — `env_mode = cfg.enforce.environment_commits`

chunk_findings.detail: The test only covers a `git merge --no-ff`, which creates a merge commit. The intent explicitly says that **squash commits must also pass**, but no test exercises that path. A squash merge is done with `git merge --squash <branch>` followed by `git commit`; the squash itself does not create `$GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD` (it records `$GIT_DIR/SQUASH_MSG` instead). The subsequent `git commit` therefore invokes the pre-commit hook exactly like a direct commit on `production`. If the implementation only checks for `MERGE_HEAD` to exempt merges, it will refuse the squash commit, violating the stated behaviour, yet the whole test suite will still pass because no test ever runs `git merge --squash` + `git commit`. Concrete reproduction: on branch `production` with `[flow].environments = ["production"]`, run `git merge --squash main` then `git commit -m promote`; the hook rejects with the environment-branch error, and nothing in this file detects it.
